4.text: In the dance and song of the geese the motions and cackling of the

5.text: white-fronted goose (Anser albifrons) are imitated. In “The Song of the

6.text: Fighting Sandpiper” (Totanus pugnax) are imitated the quaint motions of those

7.text: birds in their social gatherings during the early nesting-season.²

8.text: Songs of the long-tailed duck (Fuligula glacialis), swan, walrus, seal, and

9.text: of reindeer-rutting, are either imitative songs or are accompanied by imitative

10.text: dances. One dance is an imitation of the scraping of skins. Another is

11.text: called “The Boneless One.” Its song has the following words: “I became

12.text: boneless!” (Aˊnɪ vai! aˊnɪ vai!). The dance is accompanied by violent jerking

13.text: motions of the head and arms to pretend that the dancers have no bones

15.text: Another class of these songs represents the act of copulation, with a rather

16.text: queer dance and even with imitative sounds. The dance often ends in two

17.text: girls lying on the ground imitating sexual intercourse. Frequently young boys

18.text: also take part in the performance.

19.text: CHILDREN’S GAMES, TOYS, ETC. — Boys and half-grown young men of the

20.text: Reindeer people have a few simple games of their own. Of these may be

21.text: mentioned swinging on a rope suspended from two trees or around an upright

22.text: pole, like a merry-go-round. The Maritime people are without these games

23.text: because they live on a treeless tundra. In another game a block of wood is

24.text: suspended from a tree by a rope, and the youth try to catch it with their

25.text: small lassos. Although the block is kept constantly swinging, a good marks-

26.text: man almost never misses his throw.

27.text: The scoring runs like this: “1. I saw an elk’s track; 2. I overtook the

28.text: elk; 3. I killed it.” The fact that elk-hunting is represented, shows that the

29.text: play must be of ancient origin.³

30.text: A rather curious game represents the Raven chasing a group of small

31.text: children. At first a mother stands holding on to the children, with the Raven

32.text: opposite her. He scrapes the ground with his hands, and the following con-

35.text: Raven. I am digging a hole.

38.text: Mother. What do you want the pebbles for?

39.text: Raven. To shoot at your children.

41.text: Raven. They have spoiled my corral.
